review_evidence: Codex self-review: chapter theme, pedagogy stages, deterministic keys, unseen passages, assessment coverage, age fit, and source independence
title: Madhu's Wish
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and assessment scenes instead of copying textbook prose.

levels.title: A wish and a wiser need
levels.teaching_goal: Connect Madhu's generous action, food wish, and thirst to the main idea that wants and needs are different.

guided_check.teaching_block: A main idea joins the important events. Madhu shares food, receives a food wish, and later discovers that a mountain of snacks cannot solve thirst. These events point to learning what is truly needed.
guided_check.passage: Madhu gives half his lunch to a tired traveller. Later, every food he names appears, but no drink does. After tasting salty treats, he longs for water.
guided_check.prompt: Which idea connects the whole scene?
options: A need can matter more than a want.
accepted_answers: A need can matter more than a want.
a need can matter more than a want

bridge.teaching_block: Build the idea in three steps: kind action, exciting wish, unexpected problem. The problem often reveals the lesson.
bridge.passage: First, Ishan shares his snack. Next, he wishes for endless sweets. Finally, he becomes thirsty.

masterclass.teaching_block: A common mistake is choosing one detail as the main idea. 'There were sweets' is only a detail. The main idea must explain why the wish did not fully help.
masterclass.passage: Madhu can call for fruit, laddoos, and savoury snacks. Still, his dry throat makes him unhappy.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer states an idea rather than one food detail?
options: Having many treats does not meet every need.
accepted_answers: Having many treats does not meet every need.
having many treats does not meet every need

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the new story moment and state its main idea without choices.
independent_check.passage: Rupa fills her bag with toys for a long walk. Halfway home, the bag feels heavy, and she wishes she had carried a water bottle instead.
independent_check.prompt: What main idea does Rupa's experience show?

concept_slots.description: State that a need may matter more than a want.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the wants-and-needs idea in a school setting.
transfer_check.passage: For art day, Neel packs six glitter pens but forgets his plain pencil. When the teacher asks the class to sketch first, Neel cannot begin.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain what Neel learns from this situation.

concept_slots.description: Identify the extra item Neel wanted.
Identify the item needed for the task.
Explain why the needed item mattered.

levels.title: Follow the wish step by step
levels.teaching_goal: Use time clues to arrange the wish, the feast, the thirst, and the request for water in a sensible order.

guided_check.teaching_block: Sequence words show order. First Madhu helps someone. Next he receives a wish. Then food appears. Finally he asks for water.
guided_check.passage: (1) Madhu shares lunch. (2) He is offered a wish. (3) Bowls of food appear. (4) He asks for water.
guided_check.prompt: Which event happens just before Madhu asks for water?

bridge.teaching_block: Find the starting event, then the result. A wish must be made before its result can appear.
bridge.passage: Kavi says, 'I wish for mangoes.' A basket of mangoes appears.

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not arrange events by sentence length. Use cause and time: thirst comes after eating salty food, so asking for water comes later.
masterclass.passage: Madhu tastes a salty snack. His throat feels dry. He calls for water.
options: tastes, feels thirsty, calls for water
calls for water, tastes, feels thirsty
accepted_answers: tastes, feels thirsty, calls for water

independent_check.teaching_block: Put the unseen events in a sensible order.
independent_check.passage: Words: asks for water / eats spicy peanuts / feels thirsty
independent_check.prompt: Write the three actions in order.
accepted_answers: eats spicy peanuts, feels thirsty, asks for water
eats spicy peanuts feels thirsty asks for water
eats spicy peanuts then feels thirsty then asks for water

transfer_check.passage: Words: opens umbrella / dark clouds gather / rain begins
transfer_check.prompt: Write the events from first to last.
accepted_answers: dark clouds gather, rain begins, opens umbrella
dark clouds gather rain begins opens umbrella
dark clouds gather then rain begins then opens umbrella

levels.title: Taste clues unlock words
levels.focus: infer food word meanings from context
levels.teaching_goal: Use taste, texture, and situation clues to understand and use food words such as savoury, feast, and refreshing.

guided_check.teaching_block: A nearby clue can explain a new word. In 'The savoury kachori tasted salty and spicy,' the words salty and spicy explain savoury.
guided_check.passage: The savoury snack was crisp, salty, and filled with peas.

bridge.teaching_block: Look on both sides of the new word. A large meal with many dishes is called a feast.
bridge.passage: The family spread rice, vegetables, fruit, and sweets for a feast.

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not choose a meaning because it sounds familiar. Check the sentence. Refreshing describes something that makes a tired or thirsty person feel better.
masterclass.passage: After the hot walk, the cool lemon water was refreshing.
masterclass.prompt: What does refreshing mean in this sentence?

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the context clue in the new sentence.
independent_check.passage: The hikers were famished, so they quickly finished every sandwich in the box.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use a context clue outside a food-wish story.
transfer_check.passage: After football practice, Meera took a long sip from her bottle and felt refreshed.

levels.title: Join the feast ideas
levels.teaching_goal: Use and to add, but to contrast, and because to attach a clear reason.

guided_check.teaching_block: Connectors show how ideas relate. 'Madhu ate fruit and sweets' adds. 'He had food, but he wanted water' contrasts. 'He drank because he was thirsty' gives a reason.
guided_check.passage: Madhu found bananas ___ guavas on the table.
guided_check.prompt: Which connector adds a second fruit?

bridge.teaching_block: Ask what the second idea does. If it is surprising or different, use but.
bridge.passage: The tray was full of food, ___ the jug was empty.
bridge.prompt: Which joining word marks the unexpected difference?

masterclass.teaching_block: A common mistake is putting because before a result instead of a reason. In 'He drank water because he was thirsty,' thirst is the reason.
masterclass.passage: Madhu reached for the jug ___ his throat felt dry.
masterclass.prompt: Which connector correctly introduces the reason?

independent_check.teaching_block: Choose the connector without a hint.
independent_check.passage: The soup smelled good, ___ it was too hot to taste.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Join two ideas in a new context with a complete sentence.
transfer_check.passage: The class moved indoors. Rain began heavily.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence that joins the ideas with because.

concept_slots.description: State that the class moved or went indoors.

levels.title: Write a thoughtful wish
levels.focus: write a reason and a brief lesson
levels.teaching_goal: Write a meaningful wish with a reason, then summarize what a character learns in one or two clear sentences.

guided_check.teaching_block: A thoughtful wish names what is wanted and why it helps. Worked example: 'I wish for a shaded water station because walkers could drink and rest.'
guided_check.passage: A neighbourhood playground has no drinking tap, and children carry empty bottles home.
guided_check.prompt: Which wish includes a useful reason?
options: I wish for a water tap because children need safe drinking water.
accepted_answers: I wish for a water tap because children need safe drinking water.
i wish for a water tap because children need safe drinking water

bridge.teaching_block: Build the answer in two parts: wish + because + benefit. Check that the words after because explain the wish.
bridge.passage: Wish: a fruit basket for the clinic. Benefit: waiting children can have a healthy snack.
options: because waiting children can have a healthy snack
accepted_answers: because waiting children can have a healthy snack

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not retell every event when asked for a lesson. A summary keeps the change: Madhu wanted endless food, faced thirst, and learned to value water.
masterclass.passage: Madhu enjoys a magical feast, becomes thirsty, and finally asks for water.
masterclass.prompt: Which summary keeps the important change?
options: Madhu's food wish teaches him that water is an important need.
Madhu sees plates, bowls, spoons, and a tree.
accepted_answers: Madhu's food wish teaches him that water is an important need.
madhu's food wish teaches him that water is an important need

independent_check.teaching_block: Write a useful wish for the unseen situation and explain it in your own words.
independent_check.passage: The small library becomes very dark whenever clouds cover the sun. Children stop reading even though books are available.
independent_check.prompt: Write one wish that could help the library and give a reason.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Summarize a lesson from a different kind of wish.
transfer_check.passage: Tara wishes to win a race without practising. She tires halfway. The next morning, she begins short daily runs.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the lesson of Tara's experience in one or two sentences.

concept_slots.description: Mention wishing to win without practice.
State that effort or practice is needed.

items.passage: Aman spends all his coins on stickers. At lunchtime, he has no money left for fruit.
items.prompt: Which main idea fits Aman's experience?
options: Plan for needs before extra wants.
accepted_answers: Plan for needs before extra wants.
plan for needs before extra wants

items.passage: Sia carries three storybooks to the park but forgets the cap she needs in the bright sun.
items.prompt: State the main idea of Sia's problem.

concept_slots.description: State that a need should come before extras.

items.passage: Kabir divides his last orange with a new student who has no snack.
items.prompt: What quality does Kabir show?

items.passage: Mili brings a spare bottle for her friend after hearing that the water cooler is closed.
items.prompt: Explain why Mili's action is thoughtful.

items.passage: First Nia washes the grapes. Next she places them in a bowl. Last she serves them.
items.prompt: What does Nia do after washing the grapes?
accepted_answers: she places them in a bowl

items.passage: The picnic basket holds sandwiches and apples, but the water bottles remain on the kitchen shelf.
items.prompt: Name the item left on the shelf.

items.passage: A child peels a banana, eats it, and puts the peel in a bin.
items.prompt: Which action happens last?
options: puts the peel in a bin
accepted_answers: puts the peel in a bin
put the peel in a bin

items.passage: Words: shares the slices / cuts the melon / washes the melon
items.prompt: Arrange the actions from first to last.
accepted_answers: washes the melon, cuts the melon, shares the slices
washes the melon cuts the melon shares the slices

items.passage: The crisp papad broke with a light crunch.
items.prompt: What does crisp mean here?

items.passage: After missing breakfast, Rohan was ravenous and ate two bowls of rice.
items.prompt: What does ravenous mean?

items.passage: The celebration table holds rice, curry, breads, fruit, and sweets.
items.prompt: Which word names this large special meal?

items.passage: A salty snack and a sugary dessert are placed on separate plates.
items.prompt: Write the word for the salty, non-sweet kind of food.

items.passage: Leena packed juice ___ forgot the cups.
items.prompt: Which connector shows the contrast?

items.passage: The players drank water ___ the afternoon was hot.
items.prompt: Write the missing reason connector.

items.passage: The community fridge is empty. Neighbours decide to donate food.
items.prompt: Which is a complete sentence about their action?

items.passage: The school garden needs water during the holiday.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence suggesting a helpful action.

concept_slots.description: Use a complete thought with a subject and action.

items.passage: A roadside water pot is empty on a hot afternoon.
items.prompt: Which response gives a useful wish and reason?
options: I wish it were filled because travellers need drinking water.
accepted_answers: I wish it were filled because travellers need drinking water.
i wish it were filled because travellers need drinking water

items.passage: The class snack box has biscuits but no fruit.
items.prompt: Suggest one helpful wish and explain why.

concept_slots.description: Wish for fruit or a healthy choice.
Explain a health or variety benefit.

items.passage: Varun wishes for a room full of games. When the power fails, he notices that a simple torch would help his family more.
items.prompt: Which summary best captures Varun's learning?
options: Varun learns that a useful need can matter more than extra games.
accepted_answers: Varun learns that a useful need can matter more than extra games.
varun learns that a useful need can matter more than extra games

items.passage: Pihu asks for a giant cake, eats one slice, and then shares the rest with families at a shelter.
items.prompt: Summarize Pihu's change in one or two sentences.

concept_slots.description: Show movement from wanting for herself to helping others.
